newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: High winds blow over Swiss mountain railcar.
newsitem.headline: High winds blow over Swiss mountain railcar.

text.p: Winds with gusts of up to 150 kilometre (90 miles) per hour blew over a heavy railway car in the Swiss Alps, injuring four tourists, officials said on Tuesday.
The accident occurred on Monday at around 2,000 metres (6,500 feet), as around 90 tourists and workers were coming down from Europe's highest railway station at 3,454 metres (11,300 feet).
It was the first such since the rail link opened in 1893 on the Jungfraujoch mountain in the Bernese Oberland, a rail spokesman said.
"This has never before happened in the long history of the railway," said Christian Balmer, chief of operations for Jungfrau railways, a popular line for visitors to the Alps.
The injured tourists from Japan and Taiwan remained in the hospital overnight for observation.
The rail route includes spectacular views from Europe's highest rail station.
The railcar was a double locomotive weighing 50 tonnes, which had been put into use because it was heavier than the wagons normally used for the line, Balmer said.
